§7.2.4 Escaping Printed Marks

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

text-escaping-printed-marks · text formatting inline

✅ Normative

A character the page prints is content, even when Markdown would read it as syntax. It MUST be escaped so that it cannot open a span — \*\*, \_, \| — and it MUST NOT be deleted to avoid the collision.

Some marks a document prints are also Markdown's own punctuation: a menu that flags allergens with **, a form that labels a field _____, a legal citation using |. The mark is transcribed, and kept from being read as markup.

Melt-in-the-Middle Fish Pie Fishcake**      ← ** is a printed allergen marker
Beer-Battered Haddock & Chips§**               pointing at a legend elsewhere

Written unescaped, that ** opens a bold span that never closes and swallows the rest of the block.

What to escape

| Printed | Output | Would otherwise | | --- | --- | --- | | * ** | \* \*\* | Open emphasis or bold | | _ __ | \_ \__ | Open emphasis, or vanish inside a word | | # at line start | \# | Become a heading | | | inside a table cell | \| | Split the cell | | ` | \` | Open a code span | | ~~ | \~\~ | Strike the text through | | --- at line start | \-\-\- | Become a horizontal rule, or collide with the page separator | | A literal bracketed number or word — [1], [date] | \[1\], \[date\] | Read as a marker ([x], [blank]) or a form id | | A literal angle-bracket placeholder — <NAME> | <NAME> | Be read as an HTML tag and vanish |

  • Escaping SHOULD be applied only where the collision is real. A * in the middle of a word, or a # mid-sentence, needs nothing.
  • A printed character MUST NOT be replaced by a different mark to avoid the collision: rewriting ** as <sup>2</sup> or as a word is the never invent failure, and dropping it is the never drop one. The marker is the only thing tying an item to its legend; a legend entry with nothing pointing at it is unusable.

A raised marker is still a superscript

Escaping decides how the character survives; it does not decide its position. A marker printed above the baseline MUST be written <sup>\*\*</sup> — both rules apply, and neither substitutes for the other. See Superscript and Subscript§7.2.11.

Dashes, literal brackets and angle brackets

✅ Sample — lines that open with three dashes

Every sub-point on the slide begins with --- as its marker, printed bold. Left as printed, each line becomes a horizontal rule and its text vanishes into the rule above. The --- in the middle of New Strategy---Fund is not at line start and needs no escape.

✅ Sample — bracketed numbers that are not form ids

[1], [2], [3] number the sub-items of a note; the value None sits at the right. The same page carries (1), (2), (3) for the items above them, which need no escape. The bold heading *Notes opens with a printed asterisk.

✅ Sample — bracketed template placeholders

[#say on oath #affirm], [date], [name], [specify language] printed on grey highlights inside the sentences of a court template. Every one would read as a form id or a checkbox, and the grey is a highlight — see Highlighted Text§7.2.5. The italic notice [on separate page] under the page number is bracketed too.

Expected Markdown · excerpt

3

[on separate page]

…

I [#say on oath #affirm]:

  1. I am an accredited interpreter as defined in the Court Interpreter Standards Code 2019 in the following languages [provide details of the languages].

  2. My [#accreditation #registration #recognition] to interpret the languages set out in paragraph 1 has been issued by [provide details of the recognised agency].

  3. On [date] I sight translated the above affidavit of [name] dated [date] (the Affidavit) to [name] (the Deponent) in the [specify language] language.

  4. Before translating the Affidavit, I:

    a. read the code of conduct contained in Schedule 4B to the Court Interpreter Standards Code 2019 and agreed to be bound by it; and

    b. was given adequate opportunity to prepare to sight translate the Affidavit.

  5. After I sight translated the entire Affidavit to the Deponent, the Deponent then:

    a. informed the person responsible for the preparation of the Affidavit through me that the Deponent understood my interpretation and agreed with the entire contents of the Affidavit; and

    b. [#swore #affirmed] the Affidavit in my presence.

✅ Sample — angle-bracket placeholders

<LEGAL DESCRIPTION OF PROPERTY>, <AFFIANT SIGNATURE>, <TYPE NAME OF AFFIANT> on grey highlights. Left as printed, each is an HTML tag and vanishes from a rendered page. The first line is the tail of a placeholder that began on the previous page, so only its closing > is printed. The ruled lines are empty fields — see Blanks Inside Sentences§10.4.1.
